propositions: A description write verified by read-back at 14,997 chars was silently reverted to a stale 10,582-char revision without error or conflict notification.
Read-back verification passed immediately after the write but the data was later silently lost, invalidating the standard mitigation that agents are told to use.
The ticket was being edited while its own plan-review was running and emitting REVIEW_RESULT sidecar events; store reconvergence between concurrent writers is suspected.
Optimistic concurrency (ConcurrencyError/exit 10) did not fire on the losing write; instead the write reported success and was silently rolled back afterwards.
A stale whole-description EDIT event carrying older client-held text can last-writer-wins over newer valid events without explicit compare-and-swap or base revision protection.
The undocumented constraint to never write during a review conflicts with the normal revise-then-review loop that the plan-review gate instructs authors to perform.
